items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Dave McRae, an alto player, was the one who engaged some of the musicians for the big band that Fats was using: Jack Butler, Johnny (Bugs) Hamilton, Fats regular trumpet man and myself, were the brass section.

ctx.x: Jack Butler was not content to be just a member of the singing trio we had with Wilson Meyers, although we did our numbers in the Pengoin and they went over big. One afternoon Jack told Willie that he wanted to sing a number alone. He had been studying voice with some teacher in Knocke and even had a pianist who may have been the teacher to accompany him. He sang an Italian song the title of which I or no one else had ever heard.

I know that I did not have a great voice but Willie Lewis did. He had a wonderful baritone voice with plenty of power behind it. But Jack sang through his nose and most everybody in the club that afternoon was going into hysteria from laughing when Jack started singing his song. And the saddest part of the whole thing was that he was supposed to be singing in Italian. One of the waiters spoke Italian
but he couldn't understand one word of what Jack was saying. Well, after that, Jack didn't ask to do a number anymore.
